mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and higher interest rates, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 70% of instances where UNRATE increases by > 0.2pp MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand and economic expansion, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST shows sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it indicates a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth rate < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong labor market conditions, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 200k MoM and UNRATE decreases by > 0.1pp MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by > 200k MoM and UNRATE decreases by > 0.1pp MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates growing consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 70% of instances where RSAFS increases by > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) in a regime of low inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests accommodative monetary policy, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL growth rate < 2%.
